dedupe_keys.name: highway corridor landslide hazard maps for california california geological survey for caltrans

description: The California Geological Survey (CGS) prepared landslide hazard maps of selected California highway corridors under contract to Caltrans, after the 1997 Mill Creek Slide closed part of US Highway 50 for about a month. Each report describes the geologic materials along a corridor, the distribution and types of landslides and their potential impacts on the highway, with a geologic map (Plate 1) and a landslide inventory map (Plate 2). Coverage: Special Reports 184 to 196 cover Highway 101 (Del Norte and Mendocino), Highway 1 (Big Sur and Sonoma coast), Highway 60, Interstate 5 (Valencia to Gorman) and Highway 299; Special Report 243 (Phase 2) adds Routes 101, 162, 1, 84, 17, 35, 57, 142, 241 and 261, with susceptibility, seismically induced and combined hazard plates for Route 84. Format and access: PDF reports and map sections sized for 11x17 inch printing, downloadable from the CGS page. Licence and cost: free to download; no licence is stated on the page. Caveats: maps are PDFs, not GIS layers, and corridors were mapped at different dates. The maps support hazard exposure and resilience studies of highway links, for example to flag landslide-prone segments in a network model. It relates to the US Landslide Exposure Database and the Caltrans traffic census in the catalogue.
